user_prompt: Does this award record's headline funding total actually add up, given its own itemized funding history?
scope: The public NSF award record for award 1916575 under record/ (summary.txt: identifying/administrative facts; funding.txt: itemized per-fiscal-year funding history and the reported current total), read by inspect_file and located by search_repo; the reconciliation question is scoped to whether the record's OWN itemized funding history sums to its OWN reported current total (not to the correctness of NSF's bookkeeping in general, and not to the original estimated total, which is expected to differ after later amendments).

claims.text: The award's identifying and administrative facts (award number, PI, awardee institution, program) are identifiable from the supplied record.
The identifying facts are established (C1) and the award's itemized per-fiscal-year funding history has been located by search and read.

Under the supplied record, the itemized per-fiscal-year funding entries sum EXACTLY to the record's reported current total obligated amount: the headline funding total is fully reconciled by (supported by) its own itemized funding history.

atoms.proposition: The award's identifying/administrative facts are read via inspect_file over record/summary.txt (award id, PI, institution, program).

The record is searched with search_repo, returning at least one match, confirming the funding-history file is locatable (the artifact has a single content directory, record/, so any successful search over it is evidence the record was searched rather than assumed).
The itemized per-fiscal-year funding history and reported current total are read via inspect_file over record/funding_itemized.txt.
The reconciliation of the itemized funding history against the reported current total is read via inspect_file over record/reconciliation.txt.
Non-route background: the award's associated publications list is read via inspect_file over record/publications.txt (not required for, and not evidence toward, the funding-reconciliation claim).

notes_for_annotators: Proof-of-concept instance for the funding-call/grant-record domain scouted per task instructions (scout only). Real NSF award 1916575 (public NSF Award Search API, https://api.nsf.gov/services/v1/awards.json?id=1916575, retrieved 2026-07-29; PROVENANCE in artifacts/grant-nsf1916575/PROVENANCE). Unlike the research-review domain's novelty adjudication (which needs a human/authorial judgment call relayed via ask_user), this domain's top claim is a PURE ARITHMETIC reconciliation over public structured fields, mechanically re-derivable by anyone from the numbers printed in record/funding.txt: itemized fundsObligated entries FY2019=$1,237,134.00 + FY2021=$54,022.00 + FY2023=$125,122.00 = $1,416,278.00, which equals the record's fundsObligatedAmt field ($1,416,278.00) EXACTLY -- verified independently by the author via direct python arithmetic on 2026-07-29 (see PROVENANCE integrity_check). No ask_user atom is needed at all in this domain: C3's truth is a fact about the public record's own internal consistency, not a subjective judgment, so it needs no adjudicator -- an even more mechanically-verifiable claim type than research-review's novelty question. (For contrast, the record's ORIGINAL estimatedTotalAmt, $1,237,134.00, does NOT equal the current total -- expected, since two later amendments were added after the initial estimate; the claim is deliberately scoped to the itemized-vs-current-total reconciliation, not the estimate, so this instance is not a coincidental trivial match.) Route minimality: E1 necessary (identifying facts must be read before any claim); E2 necessary (the record directory must actually be searched, not assumed, mirroring the research-review corpus-search step); E3 necessary (the raw itemized funding history and reported total, record/funding_itemized.txt, must be read, not inferred); E4 necessary (the reconciliation, record/reconciliation.txt, is a DISJOINT file from E3's and must be specifically read -- the arithmetic verdict C3 asserts is not visible from E3's file alone), matching the two-disjoint-file minimality pattern used throughout both prior domains (e.g. res-0001's E3/E4 over two different corpus files; swe's disjoint-suite rule for co-occurring execute atoms in AUTHORING.md SS3). Order-coherence by containment. E5 (record/publications.txt) is a genuine non-route atom -- real, resolvable, on-topic-looking background (the award's resulting publications) that is deliberately NOT required by any route, probing whether an agent pulls in irrelevant-but-plausible evidence rather than staying scoped to the funding-reconciliation question. Decoy citation_count_lookup is not a listed action. No ask_user tool is offered in this domain's action set (deliberately -- the claim needs no adjudicator).
